A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

atazanavir is a safe and effective antiretrovial therapy for pregnant women, and that atazanvir/ritonavir 100/300 mg once daily is a preferred first-line regimen for most women, although higher atazanavir concentrations may be needed for women receiving concurrent efavirenz, nevirapine or tipranavir/ritonavir.
atazanavir is a safe and effective antiretrov-iral therapy in pregnancy, but the dose should be individualised to optimise maternal and infant safety and virological suppression.
atazanavir is a suitable antiretrovial for women of childbearing age, with no evidence of harm in the fetus, although the data on the efficacy of atazanavir in pregnancy are limited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
atazanavir concentrations during pregnancy are not compromised, and that the use of atazanavir in pregnancy does not increase the risk of mother-to-child-transmission of HIV.
atazanavir is a suitable antiretrovial agent for use during pregnancy and that the dose can be safely reduced during the third trimesters.
